How to Use This Dictionary

Methodology

This document is the system of record for how Salesforce works at Healthie. It catalogs the key fields across seven Salesforce objects, where each value comes from, who owns it, what depends on it, and how confident we should be in it. Use it as a reference when building reports, debugging data issues, onboarding new team members, or proposing schema changes.

Fields were selected based on actual population rates from a sample of 200 recent records per object. Population Rate (Pop %) indicates what percentage of sampled records have a value in that field. Color coding:

Green (80%+): widely used, reliable for reporting and segmentation.

Orange (50-79%): moderately used; verify before relying on for critical reports.

Red (<50%): sparsely populated but operationally relevant; usually conditional or in-progress fields.

Fields with <10% population or that are purely internal/legacy have been excluded. The TaskRay Project object had only 1 record at time of audit, so its population rates are not statistically meaningful (marked with *).

Each per-object table follows this structure:

This dictionary is intended to be a living document. Suggested cadence:

Quarterly: re-sample population rates, refresh "Last Reviewed" dates per object, audit for new/deprecated fields.

On schema change: any new SFDC field added, picklist value modified, or integration changed should trigger a changelog entry.

Annually: full re-audit, including picklist value enumeration and dependency mapping.

Column Definitions
ColumnWhat it captures
Field LabelDisplay name in Salesforce.
Data TypeSalesforce field type (Text, Picklist, Formula, Lookup, Roll-Up Summary, etc.).
Pop %Percentage of sampled records with a non-null value (color-coded).
Source / UpdateWhere the value comes from: manual entry, formula, integration sync (Stripe, Healthie, Hubspot, AskNicely, Chameleon, Apollo, Clay/Zapier, Vitally), Salesforce flow, or roll-up. Critical for debugging — knowing whether to chase the rep, the integration, or the formula author is half the battle.
OwnerTeam or individual responsible for the field's accuracy and definition. RevOps is the catch-all unless otherwise specified.
SensitivityPII / Financial / Financial ID / Internal. Guides handling, especially in shared reports and exports.
DescriptionBusiness definition of the field, including picklist values where known.
Dependencies / NotesDownstream reports, automations, formulas, or integrations that rely on this field; known gotchas; deprecation flags.
Governance
AreaOwner / Process
Dictionary maintenanceRevOps (Director: Bill Coffin).
Picklist value additionsSubmit a RevOps Case in Salesforce; RevOps adds the value.
New field requestsSubmit a RevOps Case with use case, intended source, and downstream dependencies.
Field deprecationFlag in dictionary as [DEPRECATED]; communicate sunset date; retain for one quarter before deletion.
Integration sync changesCoordinate with respective owner (Stripe/Finance, Healthie/Engineering, Hubspot/Marketing, etc.).
Lead Scoring formulaAaron (RevOps) — see Lead Scoring Plan.
Commission formulasRevOps + Finance — see Commissions Process 2026.
Customer Health ScoreRevOps + CS — see Customer Health Score Demystified.
